rationale: The minimal covering-StopSign witness shows an inflated accepted index, but without a control it could be read as any StopSign-carrying sync raising the index. This experiment runs the same follower and the same StopSign-carrying payload with sync_idx 2, so the prefix stops just before the StopSign instead of covering it. If the diagnosis is right the accepted index stays 3, the marker remains at index 2 and is_reconfigured stays Some; only the covering prefix should inflate the index.

scope.description: Five OmniPaxos instances. Node 1 is made leader, appends entries 1 and 2 with full delivery, then reconfigures so every node accepts entries 1..2 and the StopSign. Node 5 is moved to Prepare under ballot 2 and receives an AcceptSync whose log_sync has sync_idx 2, an empty suffix and the StopSign, so the prefix stops before the marker's position.
assumptions: This is the same construction as the covering witness with sync_idx reduced from 3 to 2.
A correct sync rewrites the two entries and places the StopSign immediately after them, leaving accepted at 3.
No snapshots or trimming are involved.
excluded: Randomized loss, leadership churn, the next configuration being started, snapshots and flexible quorums.

experiment.prefix: The test acceptsync_before_stopsign_keeps_accepted builds five nodes with build_node, settles, calls try_become_leader on node 1, appends Value(1) and Value(2) with a full settle after each, then reconfigures to configuration_id 2 and settles. It sends node 5 a Prepare for ballot {config_id 1, n 2, priority 0, pid 9} with decided_idx 3 and accepted_idx 3, followed by an AcceptSync with that ballot, SequenceNumber {session 1, counter 1}, decided_idx 3 and a LogSync with sync_idx 2, an empty suffix and the StopSign for configuration_id 2. It then emits after_sync with accepted, decided, is_reconfigured and the entry kinds at indices 2 and 3.

comparisons.description: A StopSign-carrying sync whose prefix stops before the marker keeps the accepted index at three positions.
